title: The Case of the Colorful Clues
markdown:
Dawn broke. Brilliant apricot and rose streaks painted the sky. Rafi blinked awake. A tiny dynamo buzzed in his chest. Sparkle-Shine day. His invention polished anything to a dazzling shine. He bounced out of bed, feet thumping a happy rhythm on cool wood.

Then a cold splash. The Sparkle-Shine was not on its polished stand. Not under the workbench. Not behind the tool chest. Nothing.

“Cora!” His voice was tight. A flash of black feathers. A quick chirp. Cora the jackdaw landed on his desk, bright eyes wide, head cocked. “Shiny gone?” she squawked.

“Vanished. Completely. Poof.”

Cora hopped. Desk to shelf. Pecks. Taps. Loose screws scattered. Tiny bolts tinkled. Rafi’s heart raced. This was not helping. “A disaster,” he moaned.

A soft tap at the workshop window. Ms Lin, kind neighbour, framed by a warm smile. “Trouble brewing, Rafi?” A gentle breeze of a voice.

He explained, words tumbling. She nodded, gaze calm. She saw the scene. “Perhaps we need to look differently. Not just where it should be, but where it might have gone.”

Cora stopped pecking. Sharp eyes spotted something. Tiny iridescent beads. A definite trail. Not scattered. Deliberately laid. Each bead marked a spot. A planned path. “Look! Look!” She flapped a wing. They led out the open door into the bright garden.

Rafi followed. Worry melted. Curiosity surged. He bent down. A perfect line. He picked one up. Cool. Smooth. “The colours. Different at each spot. Red, then blue, then yellow. An exact message.”

Cora took flight, a little black scout plane. Circling. “More beads! Over there!” Towards a tricky tangle of garden hose. Rafi stepped where she indicated. Nudged the coiled hose. Underneath, nestled in damp earth, another bead. Yellow. Then a new sequence. Green. Orange. Purple.

“A pattern. A specific sequence. Each colour means something. We have to follow them. In the exact order.” A brilliant spark. “Like a set of instructions you must not shuffle.”

Cora tilted her head. The idea sounded new. Strange. Useful.

“A recipe, but for a task. Miss a step, or do them backwards, and you don’t get the shine.” He looked at the bead trail, then at her eager face. “You found the steps, Cora. You followed them.”

Together they followed the bead-path. Red, blue, yellow: nudge the watering can. Green, orange, purple: step over the trowel. White, pink, gold: past a hidden corner, not through the compost heap that looked like a shortcut. Cora hopped ahead and waited when the next colour had not yet appeared, as if she understood that skipping was cheating. The sequence was crucial. Miss a step. Wrong order. No Sparkle-Shine. A thrilling challenge, and a strangely comforting one: there was a right next bead, if they were patient enough to find it.

The trail ended at the old oak. High up, nestled on a sturdy branch, sat the Sparkle-Shine, gleaming in the morning sun. A small note fluttered. “For successful retrieval: follow the precise sequence. Congratulations, Technician Rafi.”

He gasped. Beamed at Cora, heart pounding. “You helped me decode it.”

Cora puffed her chest. “Steps! Shiny found!”

Ms Lin smiled from her porch. A gentle nod. “Looking differently. Following steps carefully.”

Rafi retrieved his invention. Held it tight. A wide grin spread. “Incredible. An algorithm. Ordered instructions. A secret powerful language for machines — and for finding a shine that someone hid on purpose.” His mind was buzzing. He could build so many more amazing things, if he wrote the steps as carefully as the beads had been laid.

With a determined nod, Rafi and Cora turned toward the workshop. The Sparkle-Shine glinted. The adventure was just beginning, and the next machine, he thought, would only work if the steps stayed in line.
characters: Rafi (a young technician), Cora (a jackdaw), Lin (a supervisor)
